status: Implemented local production workflow; AWS/host deployment measurements are external acceptance gates.

sets.P: eligible CONFIRMED or REPLACEMENT_CONFIRMED registration units
sets.O_p: legal one-seat or approved two-seat options for p

rank_mapper.algorithm: Keep full order; remove disabled; compact active ranks. No renormalization.

variables.z[p,o]: Boolean registration p selects option o
variables.boundary[g]: Integer row boundary between consecutive tier/contribution groups
variables.gap[a,b]: Boolean outer seat b occupied while available inner seat a empty (repair only)

hard_constraints.C1: For each eligible p: sum_o z[p,o] = 1. No variables for ineligible registrations.
hard_constraints.C2: For each physical s: occ[s] <= 1, including both seats of Emperor options.
hard_constraints.C3: Blocked seats are absent from all O_p.
hard_constraints.C4: Input schema and semantics validate unique coordinates/IDs, bounds, sides and row indices; candidates reference supplied physical seats only.
hard_constraints.C5: Only CONFIRMED / REPLACEMENT_CONFIRMED are allocated; excluded statuses reported separately.
hard_constraints.C10: Each Emperor option is one approved adjacent same-row two-seat pair; display primary name twice if guest absent.
hard_constraints.C11: Approved pairs do not straddle the centre aisle; physical positions define adjacency.
hard_constraints.C12: For tier(i) preceding tier(j), row[i] <= row[j]; equal boundary rows allowed. No tier-exclusive row ownership.
hard_constraints.C13: Same tier and contribution[i] > contribution[j] imply row[i] <= row[j]. Consecutive group boundary encoding implements C12+C13.
hard_constraints.C15: Initial/regenerate/full: row occupancy equals min(remaining physical demand, available row capacity), scanning front to back. Repair: not enforced.
hard_constraints.C16: Initial/regenerate/full: occ[outer] <= occ[inner] on each side over available seats. Repair: gaps are scored, not forbidden.
hard_constraints.C17: Accessible single must occupy an approved side position; accessible pair must have both seats accessible. This never becomes a configurable preference.

C6.tier_bonus: b_p = 100*(2-tier_index_p), except b_p=0 for accessibility-required registrations
C6.common_desirability: d_o = 2*mean(priority_rank(s)-1 for s in o); integer for one-seat and two-seat options
C6.note: Shared-tier centre preference appears once here, never as a hard condition. A fixed bonus can affect pure-tier partial-row seat desirability as well. No separate pairwise inversion cost.

C8.unit: per registration mean, not double the influence for an Emperor pair

soft_constraints.normalization: N(raw,max)=floor((200*raw+max)/(2*max)); max is clamped to at least 1
soft_constraints.all_off: Ordinary weighted stage is identically zero; all hard rules and protected repair stages remain.

repair.baseline: latest explicit published version, resolved by server; client seat maps rejected
repair.changed_units: status, tier, contribution, accessibility, category, activity or replacement linkage changed; old seats now blocked/inaccessible; added/removed registrations
repair.R1: sum moved[p] for unaffected surviving registration units
repair.R2: sum doubled-centroid Manhattan distance over all surviving previously assigned units
repair.R3: number of all inner/outer occupancy inversions over available same-side seats
repair.scope_note: Last scope includes all assignable rows to permit a new numbered-section boundary; hard tier/contribution precedence remains. Unaffected units outside current scope are frozen. Escalate only on INFEASIBLE, never UNKNOWN.
repair.optimality: Only within chosen scope; scope-first repair is not a proof of globally minimum movement across scopes.

proof_and_canonicalization.budget: one shared deadline across construction, scopes, business stages and canonical passes
proof_and_canonicalization.stage_fixing: Only fix a stage objective after OPTIMAL. Stop with incumbent on FEASIBLE or later timeout; no claim about unreached stages.
proof_and_canonicalization.canonicalization: After all business objectives proven and fixed, sort participant IDs and minimize each selected option index in sequence. Sort options by stable seat IDs. Fix each index only after optimal proof.
proof_and_canonicalization.completion: canonicalization_complete is true only when all passes finish. OPTIMAL describes business objectives; canonical completion is separate.
proof_and_canonicalization.strict_mode: require_optimal=true rejects unproven business objectives; production default accepts independently valid FEASIBLE.

independent_validation: production_validator.py reconstructs physical assignment rules and all displayed scoring from source_request and baseline_snapshot, checks representations and objective-stage values; it does not claim to independently re-prove CP-SAT bounds.
lifecycle: Immutable snapshot; DRAFT -> UNDER_REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PUBLISHED. Atomic published pointer/supersession. Manual edit produces a freshly scored draft with MANUALLY_MODIFIED current status and retained generation provenance.
legacy: v1 modules/config fixtures are reproduction-only and not used by the production API.
